sec: Group II hormones: second messengers and GPCR mechanism · p834

items.q: Group II hormone actions are mediated through:
items.exp: Group II acts through second messengers affecting transport channels, protein translation, modification and gene transcription. (Book p834)

items.q: Which is NOT one of the four Group II receptor types listed?
items.exp: Group II receptor types are GPCR, TKR, JAK/cytokine receptor and STKR; the intracellular steroid receptor is Group I. (Book p834)

items.q: On hormone binding to a GPCR, the α subunit undergoes which nucleotide change?
opts: GDP converts to GTP and α dissociates to attach to the effector
GTP converts to GDP and α stays bound
ATP converts to cAMP on α
items.exp: GDP converts to GTP; the α subunit dissociates from the complex and attaches to the effector, activating it. (Book p834)

items.q: Match G-protein to second messenger — 1) Gs/Gi  2) Gq  3) Gt … A) IP3/DAG  B) cAMP  C) cAMP via transducin
items.exp: Gs/Gi signal via cAMP, Gq via IP3/DAG, and Gt (transducin) via cAMP. (Book p834)

items.q: cAMP exerts its effect by converting inactive PKA to active PKA, which then causes:
items.exp: cAMP activates PKA (protein kinase A) leading to protein phosphorylation and effects. (Book p834)

items.q: In the Gq pathway, phospholipase C cleaves PIP2 into:
items.exp: Phospholipase C splits phosphatidylinositol pyrophosphate (PIP2) into DAG and IP3. (Book p834)

items.q: Match the Gq second messenger to its target — 1) DAG  2) IP3 … A) Activates Ca2+/calmodulin pathway  B) Activates PKC (protein kinase C)
items.exp: DAG activates PKC; IP3 activates the Ca2+/calmodulin pathway. (Book p834)
